Let me start by saying this: Foxhole is a good game. The concept is brilliant, a persistent, player-driven war where every bullet, tank, and trench is built and fought over by real players. The scale is impressive, the community is passionate, and I can absolutely see why people sink thousands of hours into it.

But it's not for me.

I play solo and have limited time, and this game is brutally unforgiving to players like me. You hit a hard ceiling fast, you're not capturing towns, running effective logistics, or making any real impact by yourself. Playing with a squad makes life exponentially easier, but I don't want to be glued to a clan every single session just to feel like I'm progressing.

Sure, you can drop in and out freely, but the second you log off without a group, you're right back to being a lone cog in a machine that doesn't care about you. 2 Hours is not enough to really understand the game, and by the time you have done 2 hours you cannot refund the game.

Foxhole is a great game. Honestly. Just not for solo casuals like me. If you have a regiment and unlimited time, dive in. If you're a lone wolf with a job? Think twice. Maybe in the future when I have more time I'll change the review but for now I cannot experience it "fully" without going over my hours.

citations.review_text: i can talk with anyone because of a voice chat error that's almost impossible to fix and almost always server side and when it does work its very spotty idk what to do.

I just wanted to review to balance the field a bit. I think most of the recent negative reviews seem to be from when the developers added a half cooked aerial combat update / a salty dev comment. Seems I've joined after they've pushed another that adds the needed anti air systems, though yes, it could still do with some polish. I thought it would be a good idea to give a thumbs up to give a lil love to the dev team so they don't get disheartened and abandon the project... I'm seeing some negatives from people that have put 1000 hours into game / still actively play, and it seems like the community is basically shooting themselves in the foot by review bombing.

From my limited time in game so far, it's well worth a buy for the price.

When I joined, some people accused me of being like a spy for the enemy team. Apparently there's a multi accounting issue where some sad no life people buy more copies of the game to sabotage the other team rather than trying to get good themselves. Once I started helping out and got some commends, everyone has been really nice and helpful.

I think honestly the main point of friction for me is the equipment UI.
You have to do some juggling. For example if you want to use a medkit, you have to 'load the bandages' into it, but there's no way to load the kit like a gun so you have to unequip and equip. It's a bit dumb to say the least, I think it would be really easy for devs to add a 'reload'. They could do with making your loadouts be able to auto load mags after you spawn too. Little QoL stuff like that would be such an easy win and make gameplay much more fluid.

For the best experience, it seems you definitely need to squad up, regardless of whether you play front or back lines, you will get some good lol moments with teams.

I guess I feel that designing a game like this is a crazy task, let alone developing it. But yeah, for 20 quid... You will get your monies worth.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that logistics and crafting require massive investments of time and resources.

citations.review_text:
Ok, look. I love this game. This game is the exact niche I have wanted for all my life. I will keep playing this game. But in its current state, I just cannot recommend it. Here are the reasons why:

[h2] General Cost of Logistics [/h2]

Ok, this is one of the biggest issues the game has, and its roots extend to other larger issues. The cost of most things are literally colossal. Bigger ships usually needs upwards of 2k+ rare metal, and that is basically the GDP of three USAs in this game. And the cost, the peril to create the facilities REQUIRED to even build the ship in the first place is gigantic. First, you need a scrap mine. Go to an unoccupied scrap mine, if there is one, and build a factory. Which needs something called "Maintence supplies". This is the dealbreaker for most factories in this game. See, factories deplete these stuff by the very second. So if you wanna even create the most basic thing required for your dream fleet, you have to be logged in every day. To create ONE Naval Hull Segment, you need: PMat(processed materials)V, PMat IV, a copious number of all of these, a large assembly station that needs, you guessed it, rare metal to build, a bunch of hours-and also, this is a war game, so expect to get attacked by partisans- to even assemble, and congragulations, you have acquired one naval hull segment. OF MORE THAN TWENTY. This is IMPOSSIBLE for a single player to do. Which causes the issue I have been building up to:

[h2] The Clan Man. [/h2]

Most clans in this game, suck. Literally. There is at least 10 clans on every hex. Some large, some small, some in between. Clans dont hesitate to exploit solo players. And when they have an admin on their side? Youre as good as done. Also, they CONSTANTLY fight eachother over resource fields, the most finite thing in this game. Clans pull resources to themselves for operations that will never happen, reserve stockpiles that they will never use, and constantly claim public plots of land to themselv…
I really like this game, the barrier to entry and time that the game asks you to commit is insane however. I hope a logistics rework happens eventually as i'd hate to see a game like this die out.

The game is fun but i refuse to ever play it again ,after the infinite chances i took and all the effort made, after trying and trying to get one single good run, something always happens to ruin your plans and kills you and waist hours and days of preparing,building a ship with all its ammo takes up hours of your time...just for you to drive that boat halfway across the world map and get shot by someone in the first 30 seconds and youll lose everything , including the reason to keep playing...

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking in-game moderation and effective anti-cheat systems.

citations.review_text:
The developers don't fight cheating

I've put serious hours into Foxhole and love the concept, but there's a real problem the devs keep ignoring: cheating and sabotage go almost completely unpunished. There are no proper anti-cheat tools, no effective reporting system, and griefing/sabotage accounts run wild with basically no consequences.

You can pour hours into building and defending, only to watch it all get wiped by people abusing exploits — and the devs won't compensate the players who lost everything, or even acknowledge it. When cheaters face no risk and honest players get punished for playing fair, it drains the motivation to keep going.

Foxhole has incredible potential, but until the devs take cheating and sabotage seriously and give players real tools to fight it, I can't fully recommend it.

After 1,000 hours in the game I’d say save yourself the trouble of getting invested into the loop. The concept is cool, the grind is engaging however the development team has seemingly abandoned the game.

There is a giant lack of communication from the dev, zero in game or community moderation and rampant cheating, alt accounting and botting. It’s not a game worth picking up and getting into if you’re wanting to play fairly as intended. You’ll waste too much of your time grinding to have it stolen from rule breakers.

Game has a lot potential but unfortunately right now is riddled with hackers that openly show how they crack the game without consequences. It doesn't help that game has no in-game moderation and the developer team is radio silent.

Constant cheating. Limited to non existent communication from developers outside of occasional dev branches. Every major update though can offer unique and interesting concepts also introduce a bunch of problems. Lots of Mechanics in the game are very disrespectful of player time and investment.

I would love to recommend this game as there can be very unique experiences to be played through, however the developers are dangerously out of touch with the community. Siege camp should honestly be renamed silent camp, No community manager. 

The game is held back massively by its 'queue system' there is a good reason why experienced players will call this  'Queuehole' as spending 6 hours waiting to join a particular frontline is not unheard of, though admittedly is the extreme end. New player experience is also sadly very challenging, their isn't really a tutorial outside of the 'Home Island' and that in itself isn't very obvious to new players. You essentially have to learn off experienced players who have taught themselves or via YouTube videos. There is 0 guidance on building in the game which will often put new players in conflict with ingame groups when they try to build in areas which have importance or valuable resources.

More notably there has been consistent and reoccurring incidents of major cheating in the game recently, cheat programmes being openly advertised without little action from the developers. 

Siegecamp if you do read these (Which I have to doubt but happy to be wrong) you are in complete estrangement from your community and when you do seem to be willing to communicate its very limited and very much on your own terms. It was nice to see some modicum of responsibility taken in the wake of the disastrous airborne release and the shifting to 6 week wars to facilitate QoL updates but the fact it took mass negative reviews on Steam and a fake dev stream on Twitch to get a response from yourselves sets a dangerous precedent. 

I cant help but feel Foxh…

Really fun game that will die if nothing is done about cheaters and exploiters. Obviously implementing anti cheat won't be a silver bullet...but It's obvious this game needs some type of community manager / in game moderation to actively suspend or ban offenders. However, the devs seem to have no interest in making that happen.

I suggest if you are looking to buy this game you hold off until the Devs actually start to do something about the cheaters and exploiters.

citations.review_text:
To the Game Developers,

This is a fun game, and I’ve been playing it for quite some time. However, there are many things that I feel could be improved.

You need to understand that this game already requires much more time to play compared to other games, and the game does not do a very good job of helping new players understand how everything works.

The decision to merge the servers has also created a very obvious gap between experienced and inexperienced players. I understand that this is not necessarily the game’s fault, but it makes experienced players feel like they are wasting their time and being forced to suffer through unnecessary difficulties.

The game already demands a lot of time from players, and now experienced players also have to deal with inexperienced players who don’t understand how to play effectively. This can make the overall experience much more frustrating than it needs to be.

And this is without even mentioning the updates and the lack of balance between the two sides. Some content and changes simply do not feel fair or equal for both sides.

I really enjoy this game and want to continue playing it, which is why I hope the developers will take these issues seriously and work toward making the game more balanced, more accessible to new players, and less frustrating for experienced players.

citations.review_text:
I've enjoyed most of the 5,000 hours. This review is based off a constant nerfing of some of the fundamental elements of the game. That's why I i have finally reviewed the game, The constant nerfs that affect partisan gameplay. You think of big things like the crane change, or you think of small things like the health of the APC. Waiting five months for the para plane doors, and then having a plane that can kill a para plane in seconds, being brought out at the same time that and they finally fix the problem. These are really odd choices from the developers, and it seems like they don't value our time. Particularly like to mention the quality of life changes around facilities, and msupps, and the cost of doing it, because it feels like a second job. thats not a fun element of the game, and the devs are not really doing anything to fix it.

I'd also like to mention just briefly, alting and cheating in the game. This is something that I think the devs desperately need to address. By address, I mean fix it.

I have no clue what the devs are smoking. The game is unbalanced 95% of the time after each and every update. Asymmetrical warfare makes sense until you look at the navy and air force. In real life, once one military starts using a specific weapon/tactic that works, I can almost guarantee you the other military will adapt and start using the technology themselves. You can have asymmetry that works, but idk why the devs have such a hard on for asymmetry in ways that DONT make sense. Cough cough wardens carrier cough cough no warden CAS and no colonial torpedoe planes cough cough. I miss the old days before the navy and air force update. The game is simply not the same anymore and it's not fun.

The devs also hate logi players. Logi is essential to the game and wouldn't work without it. But the lack of QoL features is actually insane. This game is treated like a 2nd job when your a logi player. Just go play factorio instead if you are interested in logi.

There's also little to no moderation for cheaters, exploiters, or griefers. Yayyy....

Has amazing potential but the devs do very little about cheaters and there are so many bad decisions that ruin wars.

Why give this a bad review when I have played so many hours? I had a lot of fun doing logistics but it has got to the point where front lines collapse because of bad morale due to cheaters or other dev inaction. Your actions start to feel pointless as there is no one on the front line to use the equipment you made and transported. This game is not beyond saving but based on the devs previous actions that is incredibly unlikely. I will change my review if there are meaningful changes.

If you do decide to play I would strongly advise you join a regiment that has members from multiple times zones. Playing with a group of friends who only play around 6 hours at the same time in your times zone has so many disadvantages in a 24 hour game.

Let's just use one example, maintenance supplies. Anything you build needs them to not decay. If you only run a base 6 hours a day it still needs a days worth of maintenance supplies for that. A regi with 24 hour coverage is gonna produce 4 times as much for the same amount of msupps as a base that is only running 6 hours a day.

The logistics in this game is something I enjoy a lot but the combat is such a burn out inducing meat grinder with cheaters that it is killing the game.
